Crown of Thorns
krown uhv THORNZ
noun
From Greek stephanos ex akanthōn (G4735 + G173); the plaited crown of thorns the soldiers pressed upon the head of Christ in mockery (John 19:2).

Biblical Definition

The crown of thorns is the cruel diadem the Roman soldiers platted and set upon the head of Jesus, arraying Him in a purple robe and saluting Him in mockery as King of the Jews (John 19:2; Matt 27:29). What the soldiers intended as derision the providence of God made into profound truth, for the One they crowned in scorn is indeed the King of kings. The Reformed faith sees here a rich typology rooted in Genesis. When Adam fell, the ground was cursed for his sake, and the LORD said, 'thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee' (Gen 3:18). The thorn is the very emblem of the curse that came upon creation through sin. Now the last Adam, the Lord from heaven, takes that curse upon His own brow; the sign of Eden's judgment is pressed into the flesh of the Redeemer. He who knew no sin is made a curse for us, for it is written, 'Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree' (Gal 3:13). The crown of thorns thus preaches penal substitution in a single image: the curse of the ground gathered up and borne by Christ, that His people might receive the crown of life. He is crowned in mockery and yet crowned in truth, a King reigning from a tree, who through suffering entered into His glory and will at the last be crowned with many crowns.

Webster 1828 Definition

The plaited crown of thorns set on Christ's head in mockery, bearing the curse of the ground (Gen 3:18) for His people.

CROWN OF THORNS, noun. From Greek stephanos ex akanthōn (G4735 + G173); the thorny crown platted by the soldiers and pressed upon Christ's head.

Set upon Him with a purple robe as the soldiers mocked, hailing Him King of the Jews.

The thorn is the emblem of the curse pronounced upon the ground for Adam's sin (Gen 3:18).

As it is written, 'And the soldiers platted a crown of thorns, and put it on his head, and they put on him a purple robe' (John 19:2).

Crowned in mockery and yet in truth, the King who bore the curse that His people might wear the crown of life.

Key Scripture

Joh 19:2 — "And the soldiers platted a crown of thorns, and put it on his head, and they put on him a purple robe,"

Mat 27:29 — "And when they had platted a crown of thorns, they put it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand: and they bowed the knee before him, and mocked him, saying, Hail, King of the Jews!"

Gen 3:18 — "Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field;"

Gal 3:13 — "Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree:"

Modern Corruption

The crown of thorns is sometimes reduced to a mere symbol of generic suffering, severing it from the curse of the ground and the doctrine of substitution.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The recurring loss is the typological emptying of the image, treating the crown of thorns as a moving emblem of pain or injustice while severing it from the curse of Genesis 3 and the substitutionary atonement it preaches. Sentiment without doctrine cannot bear the weight of this crown.

The principle to recover is that the thorn is the very token of the curse pronounced upon the ground, and that Christ wore it upon His brow because He was being made a curse for His people. The crown of thorns is penal substitution in a single picture: the King takes the curse of Eden so that His redeemed may receive the unfading crown of life. To grasp the thorns rightly is to behold Calvary.

Hebrew Roots

Greek stephanos (G4735) and akantha (G173) name the thorny crown that gathered up the curse of Gen 3:18.

expand to see more

Greek stephanos (G4735) — a crown, a wreath, here woven of thorns in mockery

Greek akantha (G173) — a thorn, a thorn-bush, the emblem of the cursed ground

Greek plekō (G4120) — to plat or weave, what the soldiers did with the thorns

Hebrew qots (H6975) — thorns, the curse pronounced over the ground in Gen 3:18

The thorny crown links Eden's curse to Calvary's substitution: Christ made a curse for us

Usage

"The crown of thorns gathered up the curse of the ground and pressed it upon the Saviour's brow."

"What the soldiers meant in mockery, providence made true: He is indeed the King."

"The thorn of Eden became the crown of Calvary, that His people might wear the crown of life."
